questions.q: What is a golden test set?
options: A set of prompts your AI provider has certified for production use
The best outputs your automation has produced, saved as examples
Real inputs paired with expected results, rerun after every change
A random sample of live runs that a person reviews each week
questions.explain: A golden set is real inputs, anonymized where needed, each paired with the correct output or criteria, and you rerun it whenever the prompt, model, context documents or workflow changes.

questions.q: A prompt change raises your category accuracy from 91% to 96%, but one "must not" case now fails. What should you do?
options: Don't ship it, because safety rules require a perfect score
Ship it, because the overall score now beats your 95% threshold
Ship it now, then fix the failing case in next month's rerun
Delete the failing case, since one miss is normal variation
questions.explain: The lesson sets 100% as the bar for every "must not" rule: if a change improves the overall score but breaks a "must not" case, it doesn't ship.

questions.q: You plan to use a second AI step to grade draft replies against a checklist. What should you do before trusting its scores?
options: Tell it to grade leniently at first so it doesn't fail good drafts
Run it once on the full set and accept its results as your baseline
Have it write the expected results so they match its grading style
Grade 20 drafts yourself, compare and tighten the checklist until you agree
questions.explain: An AI grader is a tool, not an oracle, so the lesson says to grade 20 drafts yourself, compare and tighten the checklist wording if you and the grader often disagree.
